label: input token d during copy phase (and at t=0)
explanation: Token detector for input d, gated by phase. Fires on every copy-phase step whose input (the fed-back previous output) is d, at about 0.6-1.0 of max; this holds 91% of activation mass with precision 1.0. Strongest when d is immediately followed by another d (the first of two adjacent ds is about 0.96, the second about 0.85). Also fires weakly (about 0.22) on d as the first original token (t=0). Other original-phase d inputs fire only sporadically and weakly (0.1-0.2), mostly at early positions. Tiny weak activations on w, f, h and b. Never fires on the delimiter or at recall_idx 0. Shows no dependence on L, out_tok or next_out, apart from the weaker effect of the d token itself.

issues: Main claims hold. On the test split, in_tok==d & phase==2 has precision 1.0 and holds about 91% of activation mass. in_tok==d & t==0 has precision 1.0. The delimiter step and recall_idx 0 never fire. Rates are flat across L.

Small understatement: original-phase d at t=1 fires about 50% of the time (precision 0.50 on dev), which is more than 'sporadic'. The mass is small (about 1.9%). At t>=2, original-phase d fires at only 5-24% precision, with no clear dependence on in_first, prev_tok or to_go. That looks like scattered noise, not a systematic class.

Activation when d is not the input is negligible in the copy phase (precision 0.002). The leftover misses in the copy phase (h, f, w inputs at about 0.1) are scattered. Misses are 15% of active steps but only 4% of mass, which matches the explanation.

Not verified: the magnitude claims about adjacent ds (0.96 vs 0.85), because the tool gives no per-condition magnitudes. Splitting copy-phase d by out_tok==d does not change precision (1.0 either way).
Small improvement: adding t==1 to the predicate raises test F1 from 0.918 to 0.924 (mass recall 0.979). Precision drops to 0.93. This is a marginal change, not a refutation.
